fields.statement: QA at c7a97c9 (cycle 2) in real Rex. Built rhiza to a scratch dir; rex new a throwaway session with --cwd at the repo running `rhiza tui launch`: the layer listed ready, roadmap, show, slice, why with summaries; down+enter opened a floating 'roadmap' block showing the roadmap JSON with the 'roadmap · j/k scroll · q quit' footer, so the cycle-1 'stream is not attached (409)' failure is fixed. Then ran the installed rhiza.lua's rhiza_launch action in real Rex with `rex do -s <session> rhiza.lua --action rhiza_launch` (rex.bind line stripped so the owner's keymap was untouched): it opened a focused floating 'Rhiza apps' layer at bounds 0.3,0.25,0.4,0.5, and enter on ready closed it and opened a 'ready' modal. But that modal showed 'rhiza: no Rhiza repository in /Users/darinhaener': a pwd probe through the same rex.session.new_layer call shows a block with no cwd starts in $HOME, and rhiza.lua passes no cwd, so the launcher (and the apps, which take its os.Getwd) run outside the repo. The ctrl+a a keypress itself was not pressed in a real client.

QA at c7a97c9 (cycle 2) with a built rhiza on this repo's real model (RHIZA_ROOT/RUN/CHANGE/FOR unset). cmp shows `rhiza <op> --json` and `rhiza tui app <op> --once` byte-identical for roadmap (19626 bytes), ready (14007), and, with --change 01M62JMSW4FH8RAWSQXHC7ZPND, slice (28179), show tui-launch-key (1332) and why quick-launch-layer (37320); both exit 0. The cycle-1 gap (tui app dropped --change, exit 2) is fixed. show on an unknown handle exits 4 in both. In real Rex the roadmap and ready apps open as floating modals with the j/k scroll footer.

QA at c7a97c9 (cycle 2) with a built rhiza, REX_CONFIG at a scratch init.lua (owner lines incl. trailing spaces) and a fake rex first on PATH. rex install wrote rhiza.lua (settings launch_key ctrl+a a, BIN = the built binary, rhiza_launch action, bind) and appended one require("rhiza") -- added by rhiza rex install line; the fake rex logged `config reload`. A second install reported both files unchanged and cmp found them byte-identical. rex uninstall removed both, and cmp shows init.lua equal to the original. Real Rex loaded the written rhiza.lua via rex do and its action opened the layer.
